answer: Trust flows like water through a cedar grove: each verified identity is a root that can pass only a fixed amount of trust downstream, and every link thins the flow, so one actor splitting into a spiral of fake accounts gains no more total trust than a single root can carry. Old endorsements fade into a relic of their former weight unless renewed by real interaction, so an attacker must keep paying in genuine, observable work to keep a swarm alive — the cost grows with every identity while the reward stays capped.
